speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming the rectal bleeding and palpable mass. To better understand the nature of this lesion, have you noticed any change in your bowel habits, such as a narrowing of the stool or a feeling of incomplete evacuation after a bowel movement?

speaker: Patient
text: 45-year-old female. The patient reports a 2-week history of rectal bleeding occurring daily with bowel movements. She denies any pain with defecation and does not present with any other complaints.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your age and the presence of a palpable rectal mass with daily bleeding, this is highly suspicious for colorectal cancer. Have you experienced any unintentional weight loss or fatigue recently? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) and Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP).

speaker: Doctor
text: Since your blood work is normal, we need to determine if the mass is obstructing the bowel. Do you have any difficulty passing stool, or does the bleeding occur specifically on the surface of formed stools? REQUEST IMAGES: Proctoscopy or flexible sigmoidoscopy.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rectal bleeding daily with bowel movements. I also have No pain with defecation.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Rectal Carcinoma. Given the palpable mass, painless daily bleeding, and imaging confirmation of the lesion, the next critical step is to obtain a biopsy during the proctoscopy to confirm the pathology and stage the disease.
